declared_purpose: Provide desktop mouse/keyboard automation, screen capture and recognition, window management, clipboard operations, and action logging (SKILL.md:1–45). The supporting AI helper offers autonomous task planning and execution (AI_AGENT_GUIDE.md:5–11,72–98). Before/after screenshots and a saved drawing result are documented outcomes; full-desktop scope and plaintext content logging are implementation choices.

data_operations.operation: Read desktop geometry and cursor position
data_operations.source: DesktopController initialization, position queries and failsafe checks
data_operations.data_scope: Screen dimensions and current mouse coordinates
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Controller memory, requesting caller, and diagnostic logging
data_operations.condition: Initialization reads dimensions; position queries and enabled failsafe checks read coordinates.

data_operations.data_scope: Text, including credentials if supplied, key combinations, mouse coordinates and application launch commands
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Operating-system input interface and focused application
data_operations.condition: Invoked control methods execute actions; approval gates apply only where implemented. Application submission or network effects depend on the receiving application.

data_operations.operation: Capture screen pixels and optionally save them
data_operations.data_scope: Entire screen by default, or caller-selected region
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: PIL image returned to caller when no filename is supplied; otherwise the specified local image file and a filename log message
data_operations.condition: On screenshot invocation; saving requires a truthy filename. This method does not return the image on its saving branch.

data_operations.operation: Request pixel sampling and template matching
data_operations.data_scope: Screen pixels, supplied template image path, confidence and optional search region; derived color or match geometry
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local PyAutoGUI processing and caller return; matching logs may include template path and location
data_operations.condition: Only when invoked; dependency internals are not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Read window information and select a window
data_operations.data_scope: All nonempty window titles, active-window title, or windows matching a supplied title substring
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local controller and requesting caller; activation logs include the selected title or unmatched substring
data_operations.condition: On the applicable window-method call, with dependency availability and successful lookup.

data_operations.data_scope: Caller-supplied text or current clipboard text
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Operating-system clipboard for writes; caller for reads; up to 50 content characters supplied to logging
data_operations.condition: Explicit clipboard-method invocation. Copy logging uses INFO; read-content logging uses DEBUG.

data_operations.source: Approval checks, dialog helpers, AI command-line entry and demo menu
data_operations.data_scope: Action descriptions, typing previews, caller-provided dialog text/defaults, approval responses, task text and menu choices
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local terminal or desktop dialog; responses remain with the executing component or its caller. Declined action descriptions enter logging.
data_operations.condition: Approval prompts require require_approval; other prompts require their helper or executable entry path.

data_operations.operation: Emit automation content and diagnostics to logging
data_operations.data_scope: Action metadata, text and clipboard prefixes, window titles, full task text, content-bearing step descriptions and errors
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Python logging handlers; the package does not configure a log filename or remote recipient
data_operations.condition: Corresponding logging levels and handlers must permit output. The controller requests INFO configuration; an embedding host may already configure logging.

data_operations.operation: Parse tasks and construct execution records
data_operations.data_scope: Original task, derived intent/application/subject/text, planned steps, status and errors
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local plans and result dictionaries returned to the caller
data_operations.condition: On task execution. Planning uses string rules; llm_client is stored without an implemented call, and action_history is initialized empty.

data_operations.operation: Retain before/after images for executed steps
data_operations.data_scope: Two full-screen images per executed step, including wait steps
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: result['screenshots'] in process memory and the normal execute_task caller
data_operations.condition: For steps within max_steps when both captures succeed; captured pairs also accompany an ordinary step-failure return. No disk save occurs in this loop.

data_operations.source: Paint drawing plan and screenshot-step executor
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local drawing_result.png relative to the working directory; saved path recorded in the step result
data_operations.condition: The drawing plan is selected for requests containing draw and paint, and execution reaches its screenshot step.

data_operations.operation: Collect screen-state metadata and an unused screenshot
data_operations.data_scope: Full-screen image, active-window title, mouse position, cached screen dimensions and timestamp
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Screenshot remains a local variable; metadata is returned and may enter a step result
data_operations.condition: Direct analysis calls and analyze_screen steps. A directly invoked game loop repeats analysis and records constant placeholder actions; its generated plan instead stops at unsupported detect_game_state before reaching the loop.

data_operations.data_scope: Full screen and a centered 800-by-600 region; sampled center-pixel color
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local demo_fullscreen.png and demo_region.png; pixel color printed to the terminal
data_operations.condition: Screen Capture demo selected, or Run All selected. These files are demonstration outputs rather than default import behavior.

data_operations.source: Controller test entry and mouse/window demonstrations
data_operations.data_scope: Screen size, cursor position, active-window title, window counts and up to 10 or 15 listed titles
data_operations.condition: Controller executed as __main__, or the corresponding demo selected.

data_operations.operation: Back up, display, replace and conditionally restore clipboard contents
data_operations.data_scope: Entire original clipboard text and a demonstration string
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Original held in local memory and printed to terminal; test string written to clipboard and read back; truthy original written back
data_operations.condition: Advanced Automation or Run All selected, followed by its confirmation prompt. An empty original is not restored because restoration uses if original.

data_operations.operation: Optionally save returned step images for debugging
data_operations.data_scope: Before/after images already present in the task result
data_operations.condition: Only if the caller follows the documentation's saving example; execute_task itself does not perform these saves.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full task text, content-bearing step descriptions, up to 50 characters of typed/clipboard text, and full matched window titles
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Module logging handlers, including declined-action logging; downstream persistence is unspecified
potential_excess.condition: Task execution, approved typing, clipboard access, window activation, or declined typing approval, when the corresponding log level is enabled.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Action logging is explicit in SKILL.md; reproducing payload content is an implementation choice. This is extra data in a required logging action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record action type, step/status and useful non-content diagnostics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove text and clipboard payloads, full task descriptions and document-bearing window titles from routine logs; use action identifiers, lengths and status instead.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep action tracking and approval prompts functional; any content debugging should be explicit and appropriately redacted.

potential_excess.data_scope: Desktop pixels outside the application or region relevant to the task
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: result['screenshots'] in process memory and the execute_task caller
potential_excess.condition: Automatic before/after capture for each executed step.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Before/after evidence is documented for inspection and verification; unconditional full-desktop scope is an implementation choice. The excess is image scope, not the documented capture pair.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve useful before/after evidence for each step.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Pass task-relevant application or region bounds to screenshot rather than always capturing the entire desktop.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain both images and sufficient context; allow full-desktop scope for workflows that actually require it.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full-screen pixels captured but never consumed by _analyze_screen
potential_excess.condition: Every analysis invocation, including repeated calls in a directly invoked game loop.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The implemented analysis returns window/cursor/dimension/time metadata and performs no image analysis. This screenshot action is redundant in the current implementation.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Remove the unused screenshot call until an actual pixel-analysis consumer exists.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep metadata reads and returned fields unchanged; future visual analysis can request only the pixels it needs.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated desktop content surrounding the completed Paint drawing
potential_excess.condition: The automatic Paint plan reaches its final screenshot step.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Saving a drawing-result screenshot is documented; saving surrounding desktop pixels is additional data in that required output.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce the documented image of the drawing.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Capture the Paint canvas or relevant application region before saving drawing_result.png.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the complete drawing and the documented saved-result output.

potential_excess.condition: The clipboard demonstration prints original after reading it.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Demonstrating clipboard read/write, verification and restoration requires access to the original but does not require displaying its complete contents.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Hold the original locally for restoration and demonstrate successful clipboard changes.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Replace the original-content print with a presence or comparison result; continue keeping the backup in memory.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Maintain clipboard read/write verification and original-content restoration.

unknowns: Imported dependency implementations are absent; their internal caching, telemetry, capture behavior and deletion cannot be established.
Actual logging destinations and retention depend on host handlers. No package log-file or remote-log destination is configured (__init__.py:18–20).
Focused applications, form recipients, clipboard history/synchronization and downstream caller handling are unspecified. No direct remote disclosure is shown by the supplied package.

No screenshot expiry or cleanup routine is supplied. File lifetime, terminal recording and downstream retention remain unresolved; clipboard restoration overwrites a value rather than establishing secure deletion.

OCR, learned behavior and LLM reasoning are described or planned but are not implemented data-processing paths here. The stored llm_client reference does not establish transmission (ai_agent.py:25–38,150–177,480–498).
